reply.title: Squashing Values with a Sigmoid Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to take any number from negative infinity to positive infinity and squash it into a strict range between zero and one. A linear scale cannot do this because it grows without bound. By passing our input through an exponential function, we can bend the response into an S-shaped curve. As the input grows large and positive, the output approaches one. As it drops negative, the output approaches zero. The steepness parameter controls how fast this transition happens around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any input into a bounded range between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness parameter to see how sharply the curve transitions from flat to vertical.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how rapidly the curve transitions. Observe the output value at the fixed marker.
